channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Halts Oil Pumping on Atyrau-Samara Route After Drone Attack
item.description: Kazakhstan has suspended oil pumping along the Atyrau-Samara pipeline following a drone attack on the Samara hub. The duration of the suspension and the extent of the damage are not yet specified. This disruption impacts regional energy transit.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates National Fund Resources for Large-Scale Infrastructure Development
item.description: Kazakhstan plans a significant infrastructure modernization, allocating approximately 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund by the end of 2029. An additional 1.5 trillion tenge is designated for social projects in 2024-2027. This initiative aims to boost the economy and improve citizens' well-being.

item.title: US to Mediate Talks Between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi
item.description: The United States will facilitate trilateral talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, marking the first such meeting in nine months. Discussions will focus on ceasefire terms, security guarantees, and humanitarian issues. US special representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to attend.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Outlines National Security Strategy Emphasizing Economic Independence
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address outlines Kazakhstan's long-term development, focusing on economic growth, infrastructure modernization, and digital advancement. The strategy highlights strengthening economic independence and ensuring the reliability of critical infrastructure, including energy, transport, and water, to maintain societal stability amidst geopolitical challenges.

item.title: China and Oman Elevate Strategic Partnership Amidst Energy and Investment Talks
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with Sultan Haitham bin Tarik of Oman in Beijing, aiming to strengthen their strategic partnership. Discussions focused on enhancing cooperation in energy, investment, and technology. Both leaders expressed commitment to deepening bilateral ties and contributing to regional peace and prosperity.

item.title: Kazakhstan President's Address Priorities Explained to Regional Populations
item.description: Information groups, including members of the Kurultai, government officials, and public figures, are touring Kazakhstan to explain the priorities outlined in the President's address. Meetings were held in Astana, Almaty, and Akmola region, focusing on public dialogue regarding national development and economic reforms.

item.title: Eurasian Fund Provides Tajikistan $100 Million Loan at 1% Interest for Stabilization
item.description: The Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development (EFSR) has granted Tajikistan a $100 million stabilization loan. The funds are provided for 20 years at 1% annual interest with a 10-year grace period, supporting the country's macroeconomic stabilization and reform program for 2025-2027.

item.title: Global Diesel Reserves Hit 35-Year Low Amid Middle East Tensions
item.description: Global diesel reserves have fallen to their lowest point in 35 years due to escalating Middle East tensions, according to ADNOC chief Sultan Al Jaber. Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz are a primary driver of price increases, impacting shipping and leading to a significant decrease in global oil and LNG supplies.

item.title: German Businesses to Participate in Kazakhstan's Water Infrastructure Repair and Construction
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to involve German businesses in the construction and reconstruction of its water infrastructure. Discussions included enhancing water use efficiency in agriculture, implementing advanced German water management methods, and joint training programs. A Kazakhstan-Germany Water Hub is also proposed for technology exchange.

item.title: Young Footballers Fall Ill in Tashkent; Kazakh Parents Urge Swift Return Home
item.description: Young Kazakh footballers participating in a tournament in Tashkent have fallen ill, with parents reporting issues with medical care and accommodation. The children, aged 8-12, reportedly fell sick after eating breakfast at their hotel. Parents are requesting their children be returned to Kazakhstan as soon as possible.

item.title: US fighter jet attacks military site on Iran's Qeshm Island
item.description: US officials confirmed a US fighter jet attacked military positions on Iran's southern Qeshm Island. The Wall Street Journal reported the attack occurred Monday night as a defensive measure. This is part of a series of limited, covert US strikes against Iran in recent weeks. The incident followed a missile launch by Iran's IRGC towards a US aircraft over the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Constitution: Foundation for justice and human rights
item.description: Kazakhstan's Constitution serves as the cornerstone for justice and human rights, defining the state's structure and fostering societal harmony. The recently adopted Constitution reflects diverse viewpoints and continues the country's commitment to traditional values and human rights established since 2019. It is considered the primary document outlining the state's framework and the basis for law.

item.title: Belgian Prime Minister Resigns Amidst Budget Negotiation Failure
item.description: Belgium's Prime Minister has submitted his resignation to the King following the collapse of coalition negotiations for the 2027 budget. The government faces a €10 billion deficit, requiring either social spending cuts or tax increases. Belgium's national debt reached €735 billion (110% of GDP) in 2025, an unprecedented level. The King has asked the PM to continue negotiations.

item.title: Author Argues Pashtun Marginalization Post-2001 Fueled Taliban Resurgence
item.description: An author contends that the marginalization of Pashtuns after the 2001 Taliban collapse, driven by the Northern Alliance and limited US understanding of Pashtun society, weakened their political influence. This strategy, contradicting 'winning hearts and minds,' alienated Pashtun communities, contributing to the Taliban's gradual resurgence.

item.title: Achieving Energy Surplus is a Key Priority for Kazakhstan's Development
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has emphasized the critical role of energy sector development for the nation's competitiveness and economic independence. Discussions focused on implementing directives for stable energy surplus by 2029, accelerating nuclear power plant projects, and enhancing domestic expertise.

item.title: Kazakhstan Implements New Pilot Project for Immigrant Status and Residency Permits
item.description: Kazakhstan has launched a pilot project for obtaining ethnic Kazakh status and permanent residency. Applicants must pass a Kazakh language test and a questionnaire assessing their education, age, and work experience. A system automatically calculates scores, with a minimum of 600 points required for security checks and interviews. Those who pass can submit documents for status or residency.

item.title: Almaty's CHP-2 Gas Boiler Plant Begins Supplying Heat to City Homes
item.description: Almaty's CHP-2 thermal power plant has activated its new gas boiler, marking the first time it is supplying heat to city residences using natural gas instead of coal. This upgrade is a key part of the station's modernization, aiming to improve energy production efficiency and reduce environmental impact on Almaty.

item.title: UN Biodiversity Conference Adopts 'Yerevan Path' Roadmap for Nature Protection
item.description: At the 17th UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, nations agreed on a roadmap called the 'Yerevan Path' to accelerate nature protection efforts. The plan prioritizes achieving the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework's 23 targets by 2030, including phasing out harmful subsidies and increasing support for developing countries.

item.title: EAEU Central Banks Exchange Experience on Combating Fraud and Digital Currencies
item.description: Central banks from EAEU member states met in Minsk to discuss the current economic situation and monetary policy. Participants exchanged experiences in combating fraudulent operations, explored the use and prospects of digital currencies, and discussed virtual asset regulation. Kyrgyzstan's National Bank head presented on monetary policy measures and cyber threat countermeasures.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Russia Discuss Improving Customs Administration and Trade Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Russia held high-level talks to enhance bilateral trade and economic cooperation, focusing on industrial cooperation and customs administration. Discussions included expanding production ties, joint projects, and creating stable cross-border production chains within the EAEU. Both sides emphasized improving customs efficiency and information exchange.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tightens Car Import Rules, Mandating Newer Models and Euro-5 Standard
item.description: Kazakhstan is tightening rules for importing passenger cars, requiring vehicles to be no more than five years old and meet the Euro-5 environmental standard. These new regulations, set by the Ministry of Transport, will take effect by the end of December. Experts believe this will boost domestic car sales and production.

item.title: From Station to Parliament: How Serbian Students Drove Political Change
item.description: In Serbia's snap parliamentary elections, President Aleksandar Vučić's party lost power after 14 years. This article details how a student movement, born from a 2024 tragedy in Novi Sad, transformed into an independent political force, leading to a change in government within two years.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Minister visits Turkmenistan for bilateral talks
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Ashgabat with a delegation of diplomatic, economic, and parliamentary representatives. He held talks with Turkmen officials, discussing bilateral relations, regional events, and key economic projects, particularly in the trade and energy sectors. The visit aimed to strengthen partnership between the two countries.

item.title: Turkic States Summit in Ankara Focuses on New Cooperation Avenues and Uzbekistan's Initiatives
item.description: The 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) in Ankara, themed 'Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Action,' aimed to elevate multilateral cooperation. Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed initiatives to deepen ties in trade, economy, investment, transport, logistics, industrial cooperation, and human capital development.

item.title: International Exhibition on Turkmenistan's Industrial Development Opens in Ashgabat
item.description: An international exhibition and conference titled 'Development of Turkmenistan's Construction, Industrial, Chemical, and Energy Sectors' has commenced in Ashgabat. The event aims to enhance the country's industrial capacity, diversify the national economy, create new products for global markets, and increase the capabilities of existing enterprises.

item.title: Uzbekistan Faces Potential Data Breach Affecting Two-Thirds of Population
item.description: A hacker group named Butterfly claims to have obtained personal data of up to 27 million Uzbek citizens from a government database. The group has demanded authorities comply with their terms or the data will be sold. The Uzbek government has not confirmed or denied the alleged hack, which could include names, addresses, and biometric information.

item.title: UN Report Commends Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan for Ecosystem Restoration Efforts
item.description: A UN report highlights Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan's success in restoring degraded ecosystems and aiding endangered species recovery. Kazakhstan is recognized for reviving the Northern Aral Sea, placing it among top global efforts for inland water systems. The report notes that global restoration efforts have created over 1.1 million jobs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Vanadium Project Finds Value in Mining By-Products Like Carbon Black
item.description: Ferro-Alloy Resources is developing a vanadium deposit in Kazakhstan, also recovering molybdenum and nickel. The company is finding additional value in by-products such as its proprietary Carbon Black Substitute (CBS), uranium, and rare earth minerals. These by-products could significantly enhance future earnings beyond the primary vanadium extraction.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches New System for Safe and Profitable Labor Migration
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing a new system to ensure safe, orderly, and profitable labor migration. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Intil center, which provides language and professional training for citizens seeking overseas employment. The center aims to connect training with job placement and facilitate adaptation to new environments.

item.title: Central Asian Judicial Systems Convene for Cybersecurity and AI Training
item.description: Representatives from the judicial systems of Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan are participating in an international training course in Uzbekistan focused on cybersecurity, digital evidence, and artificial intelligence in judicial activities. The event aims to enhance cooperation and share best practices.

item.title: Unfavorable Air Quality Expected in 12 Kazakh Cities on November 3
item.description: Kazakhstan's 'Kazgidromet' reports unfavorable meteorological conditions are expected in Almaty and 11 other cities on November 3. These conditions, characterized by calm winds and temperature inversions, can lead to air pollution. Residents are advised to limit outdoor activities, especially vulnerable groups.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Receives Iranian Foreign Minister
item.description: President Serdar Berdimuhamedow of Turkmenistan met with Iran's Foreign Minister, Seyed Abbas Araghchi. Araghchi conveyed greetings from Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and emphasized Iran's commitment to developing relations with Turkmenistan. Both sides highlighted the importance of friendly relations based on mutual respect and trust.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans Strategic Uranium Reserve of 150,000 Tons by 2050
item.description: Kazakhstan's Atomic Energy Agency plans to establish a strategic uranium reserve of at least 150,000 tons by 2050 to secure fuel for future nuclear power plants. This initiative views uranium not just as raw material but as a strategic asset for economic development.

item.title: Austrian Ambassador Presents Credentials to Turkmenistan President
item.description: At the request of President Serdar Berdimuhamedow, Mejlis Speaker D. Gulmanowa accepted the credentials of the new Austrian Ambassador to Turkmenistan, Etienne Berchtold. The Ambassador conveyed greetings from Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen and expressed gratitude for the warm welcome. Both sides affirmed commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Deputy Mayor of Uralsk Fined 648,000 Tenge for Competition Law Violations
item.description: The deputy mayor of Uralsk has been fined 648,000 tenge for violating competition protection laws. An analysis by the Uralsk city prosecutor's office revealed that the city's housing and utilities department entered into agreements with design organizations for free development of project documentation, later implementing these projects with budget funds.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sets Price for Liquefied Gas and Compensation for Needy Families
item.description: Uzbekistan has established a retail price of 5,000 Uzbek soums per kilogram for liquefied gas supplied to the population. Needy families will receive compensation for up to 20 kilograms of gas monthly. This measure aims to support vulnerable households.

item.title: Turkmenistan advances state cooperation in new directions at Turkic States' summit
item.description: Turkmenistan participated as an observer in the summit of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS). President Serdar Berdimuhamedow planted saplings symbolizing friendship and planted trees at the opening of the Cultural Park. The event included cultural exhibitions and ethno-sport games.

item.title: Turkey Expands Air Connectivity with Uzbekistan, Adding New Routes
item.description: Turkish airline Pegasus Airlines is launching regular flights from Istanbul to Bukhara, Andijan, and Termez in Uzbekistan. The company is also considering flights to Karshi and Nukus. This expansion aims to enhance regional transport accessibility and attract foreign tourists.

item.title: Taliban and Belarus Discuss Expanding Trade Relations and Investment
item.description: The Taliban's Minister of Industry and Commerce, Nooruddin Azizi, met with Belarus's non-resident ambassador to Afghanistan, Alexander Ogorodnikov, to discuss expanding bilateral economic and trade cooperation. Topics included joint trade exhibitions, establishing trade centers, investment opportunities in Afghanistan, and facilitating visas for businesspeople. Belarus expressed readiness to strengthen economic ties.

item.title: Erdogan Sends Telegram to Tokayev While Flying Over Kazakhstan
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan sent a telegram to Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev while flying over Kazakhstan en route to South Korea. Erdogan recalled his state visit to Kazakhstan and Tokayev's recent visit to Ankara, wishing well-being to Tokayev and prosperity to the Kazakh people.
